subject: Severe latency and 5xx spikes — Veridian reserved pool (prod)
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@veridianbank.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@veridianbank.com
Date: 2029-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: SEV: High latency and 5xx spikes on Reserved pool (prod)

Team —

We're seeing sustained high tail latency (p95 ~ 780–1,100ms) and a spike in 5xx responses across our reserved capacity in prod starting ~06:30Z. Throughput appears to have dropped ~35% from baseline and some jobs are timing out. This is causing checkout failures and queued jobs to pile up.

We attached a small log excerpt and a couple of trace ids. Can you confirm whether the reserved pool is saturated or if this is a service degradation on your side? We need an immediate bridge and an ETA on mitigation — this is impacting our customers now.

Attachments: veridian-ops-log-snippet.txt (excerpt)

—Jamie
Jamie Liu
SRE Lead, Veridian Bank
jamie.liu@veridianbank.com
+1 415-555-0142
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@veridianbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-14T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: SEV: High latency and 5xx spikes on Reserved pool (prod)

Jamie — thanks for the signal and logs. We're standing up an immediate incident bridge (BR-9082) and pulling in engineering + CS.

Quick asks so we can scope root cause and mitigation:
- Can you share a sample request id that returned 5xx and approximate token lengths?
- Have there been recent traffic pattern changes or model config changes on your side in the last 24h?

Prelim note: our early dashboards are showing a sharp increase in queue depth and GPU utilization for your reserved pool starting ~06:25Z which points at headroom depletion rather than a control-plane outage. We'll confirm if noisy-neighbor allocation or kernel-level slowdowns are the cause.

I've attached a small snippet of the logs you sent and forwarded to infra (attachment retained in thread). Joining BR now.

Diego Fernandez
Account Technical Lead — Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.com
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-14T09:40:00Z
Subject: Escalation: Veridian reserved pool headroom depletion — immediate exec visibility

Vivek / Marissa —

Escalating now: Veridian (VER-7231) is experiencing production degradations tied to their reserved GPU pool. Summary of our findings so far (first 30 minutes):
- Observed: sustained p95 latency ~800–1,100ms, 5xx rate spike from 0.2% -> 4.6%, throughput down ~35%.
- Runtime telemetry: per-GPU utilization at 92–99% with persistent queueing; KV cache hit-rate dropped by ~28% coincident with a model variant rollout window at 05:58Z.
- Hypothesis: a model-variant rollout triggered larger context sizes and decreased cache effectiveness; combined with a shortfall in reserved headroom this pushed their pool into saturation. We also see evidence of tenant spillover from a hot job pattern in adjacent pools (noisy neighbor).

Immediate asks:
1) Approve one-time burst capacity (2 reserved nodes / 8 GPUs) for the next 6 hours to relieve queueing and buy time for a rollback or model tweak.
2) Pull procurement/finance if credits are needed for burst.
3) Prepare a quick MAP (mutual action plan) for Veridian outlining rollback, traffic shaping, and post-mortem timeline.

I've provisionally created BR-9082 and uploaded an initial metrics snapshot (initial-metrics-snapshot.png). We need an exec decision on burst within the next 20 minutes to prevent additional customer impact.

Diego
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-14T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Veridian reserved pool headroom depletion — immediate exec visibility

Thanks Diego — I can authorize a temporary burst while we remediate. High-level mitigation plan:
- Action A (now): apply targeted traffic shaping on Veridian routes (rate-limit heavy requests > 2k tokens) and enable fallback to the smaller LLM-compact variant for non-critical calls.
- Action B (next 15–30m): grant burst of 2 dedicated nodes (8 gpus) for 6 hours. I'll loop Finance for a charge cap — we should offer a partial credit depending on impact window.
- Action C (next 24h): schedule a rollback of the model-variant that increased context size OR apply a quantization profile to preserve cache hit-rate.

I'll own customer comms and MAP doc — attaching draft (MAP-proposal.pdf). Chloe, please coordinate on the bridge and verify the fallback routing change with infra. Vivek, please confirm infra can push the traffic shaping and the short-lived burst without retry storms.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 917-555-0226
Attachments: MAP-proposal.pdf
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@veridianbank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@veridianbank.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-15T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SEV: High latency and 5xx spikes on Reserved pool (prod) — mitigation confirmation

Marissa / Diego — thanks for the quick response. The burst and traffic shaping reduced queueing and the p95 dropped back to ~160–220ms overnight; 5xx has returned to baseline. Our ops team will validate over the next 24h.

We do want a formal post-mortem and request a proposal for credits given production impact (checkout failures during US morning window). Procurement is on the thread to start contracting/credit discussion — DEPT: procurement@veridianbank.com.

Also: please include the post-mortem and the MAP you mentioned. We'll need an executive readout next week (Tuesday preferred) to review root cause and compensation.

—Jamie
